title: Custom Events
definition: Extending the `EventEmitter` class to create custom objects that possess built-in event broadcasting capabilities.
simpleExplanation: Instead of creating a standalone 'radio station' (a raw EventEmitter), you make your own custom class INHERIT the radio station's powers. Now, your `UserDatabase` class doesn't just save users; it can natively broadcast `db.emit('userSaved')` directly from within its own methods.
realWorldExample: Creating a `ChatRoom` class that extends `EventEmitter`. When a user types a message, the class calls `this.emit('message', text)`, and all connected WebSocket clients instantly receive it.

basic: How do you make a class an EventEmitter?
intermediate: Why do we call `super()` inside the constructor?

answers.question: How to make a class an EventEmitter?
answers.answer: By using the ES6 `extends` keyword: `class MyClass extends EventEmitter {}`.

answers.question: Why call super()?
answers.answer: Because `MyClass` inherits from `EventEmitter`, calling `super()` executes the `EventEmitter`'s hidden constructor, properly initializing the hidden memory objects needed to store event listeners.
